formation.explanation: Leader admits commands, assigns current term/index and persists before local match. Peer workers replicate ordered prefixes, backtrack conflicts, fall back to snapshots and report successful stored prefixes. A voter-only tracker selects the majority prefix, gated by the first current-term entry. The leader copies commitment, advances membership and sends committed logs to the FSM queue; followers learn commit position from periodic append traffic. FSM callbacks complete command futures; queueing is not completion.

context.explanation: Follower contact timeout allows configured voters to campaign. Optional pre-vote precedes durable term increment and one request per voter. Receivers constrain votes using known leader, membership, term, durable vote and log freshness. A campaign-specific response channel prevents replies from prior campaigns being tallied in a new one. Majority victory creates fresh leader state and an initial noop. Higher-term RPC/reply, lease loss and committed local removal can end leadership. Pending leader operations fail on exit while previously committed FSM work retains its separate completion path. Startup reconstructs term, snapshot and later configuration history.

connection.explanation: Election log freshness and stored votes constrain who acquires authority over prior history. Each leader creates a new commitment object; late replication workers retain their old object and cannot directly populate the new tracker. New-term noop commitment establishes the prefix before configuration changes are admitted. Membership reinterprets eligible match support by voter ID, while all members retain replication workers. Log matching/truncation and snapshot reconstruction handle old work; committed commands continue through a distinct FSM queue. Verification is another authority consumer: its voter-sized threshold is currently fed by the broader replication-worker set, which is the first focused question.
